name: Vantablack Media Orphan Signal Cartridge
description:
The Orphan Signal Cartridge is a single-use broadcast device designed to transmit a compressed data package — message, file, or audio — across a wide-area signal burst that is specifically engineered to be unattributable to any sender. Vantablack Media developed it as a tool for protected-source journalism: a whistleblower or field correspondent can load the Cartridge with content, set a timed or proximity-triggered release, and walk away. When it fires, the burst mimics the signal profile of legacy infrastructure bleed — the kind of ghost transmissions that GLMZ's aging broadcast towers emit constantly — making the source indistinguishable from decades-old equipment noise.

The Cartridge is physically a small cylinder, roughly the size of a flare, with a single data input port and a mechanical timer ring. It contains no identifying markings and is manufactured from materials that resist forensic analysis — the polymer casing dissolves in water over 48 hours, and the internal components are designed to thermally self-erase after transmission. The broadcast itself is a single, non-repeating burst lasting between 0.3 and 1.2 seconds depending on data load, making it nearly impossible to triangulate with standard direction-finding equipment.

Vantablack markets the Cartridge under a press-freedom framework and has successfully lobbied for its classification as a journalism tool rather than a communications device in several jurisdictions. In GLMZ, this legal ambiguity has made it a staple not just of journalists but of anyone who needs to get information somewhere without leaving a trail. The secondary market for used — but not yet fired — Cartridges is surprisingly active, since buyers trust the single-use design to mean no prior data contamination.

specifications.data_capacity: Up to 500MB compressed; optimized for text, audio, and still images
specifications.trigger_options: Mechanical timer (1 minute to 72 hours), proximity sensor (paired device or passive human-presence), manual
specifications.signal_profile: Mimics legacy broadcast infrastructure bleed; defeats standard source-attribution at 94% confidence
specifications.self-destruct: Thermal erasure of internals post-transmission; casing dissolves in water over 48 hours
specifications.receiver_requirement: Any device tuned to receive the broadcast frequency range; decryption requires a paired key loaded at time of data input

tactical_use: Used for one-way unattributable transmission of critical information — intelligence packages, evidence, operational orders — to a receiving party without establishing any traceable communication channel. Operatives load the Cartridge, place it in a location that will be abandoned before transmission, and the burst fires autonomously. Receivers monitoring the appropriate frequency range and holding the decryption key retrieve the content. The physical Cartridge is never recovered.
cultural_context: The Orphan Signal Cartridge has a particular resonance in GLMZ's journalism and activist communities, where it is understood as a tool of last resort — used when someone has information that needs to exist in the world regardless of what happens to them. Finding a fired Cartridge casing is considered a minor omen in some districts, a sign that someone nearby had something important to say. Vantablack's branding around press freedom gives the device a legitimacy that its actual use in the field often exceeds.
known_users: Activist networks releasing evidence of wrongdoing
Intelligence operatives transmitting final reports under duress
Fixers delivering sensitive information to clients without direct contact
story_hooks: A Cartridge fires in a district the players are operating in — the content is addressed to them by name, from a sender who claims to already be dead.
A player is handed a loaded Cartridge by a panicked contact who says they can't be seen with it any longer; the timer is already running.

Vantablack Media's legal team reaches out: a Cartridge was used to transmit something that is now causing a diplomatic incident, and they need the players to find whoever loaded it before authorities trace the device back to Vantablack's supply chain.

A series of Cartridges have been firing in sequence across the city over the past week, each containing one piece of a larger message — someone is using them as a distributed dead drop for an audience that knows how to listen.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist cylinder resembling a precision flare or signal cartridge. The form factor is deliberately anonymous — no branding, no distinctive aesthetic flourishes. Its surface appears almost matte-black, absorbing light rather than reflecting it. The overall impression is clinical, utilitarian, designed to disappear into a pocket or pack without drawing attention.
physical_description.dimensions: 18cm tall, 3cm diameter cylinder — roughly the size of a large marker or distress flare
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld and pocketable; light enough for a vest pocket or cargo pouch, easily concealed in a messenger bag
physical_description.primary_material: Proprietary water-soluble polymer composite with embedded thermal-erasure circuitry; interior titanium-alloy shielding for RF isolation
physical_description.finish: Vantablack-grade absorptive surface coating; the polymer has a slightly waxy, organic texture that feels warm to the touch. No reflections under direct light — it seems to swallow illumination.
physical_description.color_scheme: Near-absolute black with subtle charcoal micro-striations suggesting internal segmentation. No accent colors or branding — visibility is actively avoided.
physical_description.interface_elements: Single recessed USB-C data input port (flush-mounted, dust-capped with a minimal polymer plug). Mechanical timer ring around the bottom third of the cylinder with tactile notches for 1-minute increments, unmarked beyond faint alignment markers. No LEDs, displays, or power indicators — intentionally silent.
distinctive_features: Recessed data port barely visible against the black finish — designed for tactile access in darkness
Mechanical timer ring with detent clicks; purely mechanical, no electronic timer display
Thermal vent slots concealed as faint horizontal scoring near the top — opens only during transmission
Absence of any manufacturer marking, serial number, or regulatory stamp — deliberately unmarked
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None visible. Vantablack Media deliberately omits all identifying marks; authenticity verified only through secure supply chain and key-pair documentation provided separately.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and sealed when new. Pre-use Cartridges show no wear. Post-transmission units are typically destroyed or dissolved; recovered casings are warped and porous, with internal components charred beyond forensic recovery.

The cartridge's vantablack surface absorbs the light, appearing as a void. Nearby: a data cable, a faint glow from a decryption key device, scattered water droplets on the bench suggesting dissolution testing. Moody neo-noir workspace, rain-slicked window visible in background showing GLMZ megastructures.
